Self-described survey with a 'methodology-centered taxonomy' of LLM agent systems.
Multi-agent corpus distillation built by the authors; claims are biomedical QA gains over baselines, not about loop control.
Iteration policy: action selection combines LLM likelihood with an offline RL critic's action values plus dynamic action rescoring per interaction demand.
RL fine-tuning and benchmark evaluation of reasoning under noisy inputs; no runtime iteration or control structure.
Self-described tutorial surveying RAG, PAL, ReAct, LangChain, fine-tuning and transformer training techniques.
Alignment Fine-Tuning with a constraint alignment loss over CoT responses; a training objective, not a runtime loop.

Essay and literature review categorising four types of LLM deception with an evaluative stance on governance.
Rubric reward models are evaluated for interpretability, faithfulness and configurable trade-offs, not for what the agent's loop does next.
Critical review of existing causal reasoning benchmarks for LLMs.
HELPER retrieves memory as in-context examples; the reported claim is 1.7x TEACh TfD state-of-the-art, a task outcome.
Behavioural study of whether LLM agents show human-like trust in Trust Games; the object is behavioural alignment, not a control mechanism.
Survey of the agent skills landscape organised along four axes, plus a proposed governance framework.
AgentGen synthesises environments and planning tasks for instruction tuning; the contribution is training data, not runtime control.
Agent-Driver is an application built by the authors; the claim is outperforming state-of-the-art driving methods on nuScenes.
Survey of RL across the LLM lifecycle, including datasets, benchmarks and tools.
Automatic prompt optimisation producing shorter prompts; the deployed prompt is used single-pass and claims are token count and accuracy.
Iteration policy: a task-agnostic outer loop that picks the next clarifying question by maximising expected mutual information and expands its state when insufficient.
Length-difference positional encoding fine-tuned to stop generation at a target token count; decoding-level, no agent loop.
Control topology: four agentic issue-resolution architectures are the controlled variable, measuring energy wasted on 'unproductive reasoning loops' (9.4x spread).
Comprehensive survey of LLM-brained GUI agents, their components, data, benchmarks and research gaps.
Husky's contribution is a unified action ontology plus trained expert models; the claim is beating prior agents on 14 evaluation datasets.

Post-training quantisation of weights and the KV cache; concerns memory and accuracy, no agent or loop.
Classification of tutor praise responses for real-time feedback, reported as F1 scores; no iterative agent control.
Loop state: an external VAD state carried across a 25-turn dialogue governs generation, with stateless vs first-order vs second-order dynamics compared for coherence and recovery.
STAgent's contributions are a tool environment, data curation and a SFT/RL training recipe; the claim is TravelBench performance.
ElliottAgents is a domain system the authors built; claims are pattern recognition and interpretable market predictions.
Benchmarking five LLMs on 166 ICPC problems for correctness and efficiency; one-shot generation quality, no loop.
Benchmark of agents that measures SOP and constraint adherence pass rates, not a loop property such as stuck loops, termination or retries.
Compares base, custom and fine-tuned GPT classification accuracy against human coding of ESG papers; no iterative control.
Lang-PINN is a pipeline built by the authors; reported claims are PDE solution MSE, execution success rate and time overhead.
Evaluates 13 open-source LLMs in a RAG setup on context relevance, faithfulness and answer relevance; retrieval is single-pass.
Trial-and-demonstration is a training regime for word acquisition from scratch; the loop is in learning, not in a deployed agent.
Loop state: reports systematic failures managing long-horizon context and task-state hallucination, then adds explicit belief state representations and measures the effect.
Zero-shot chain-of-thought classification of class membership, scored by F1; single-pass prompting.
LLMs used once as raters of palliative care conversation quality on metrics like understanding and empathy; no loop.
Causal Agent wires causal tools, memory and reasoning together; the claim is above-80% accuracy on the CausalTQA benchmark and a 6% gain on QRData.
A self-generated cross-modal data construction strategy for training an audio LLM; benchmark performance, no runtime loop.
Feedback-conditioned refinements are generated to build fine-tuning data for summarisation; the refinement is offline, not an agent's runtime loop.
The agents explained are robots and other uninterpretable policy models, not language-model agents; the contribution is natural-language explanation of their behaviour.
